title: Finite open exchange commutes with coefficient restriction and tower transitions
statement:
Let $(j:U\hookrightarrow X,j':U'\hookrightarrow X',g:X'\to X,g_U:U'\to U)$ be a cartesian open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square], and let $a:B\to C$ be any homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Use constant coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, the inverse images of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_a$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and exact sheafified extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Let
$$\beta_B:g_B^*j_!^B\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!{}^B g_{U,B}^*,\qquad \beta_C:g_C^*j_!^C\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!{}^C g_{U,C}^*$$
be the canonical complex-level exchanges of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change], using finite constant-coefficient module pullback [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. The canonical scalar-restriction identifications for the inverse images and extensions identify
$$\operatorname{Res}_a(\beta_{C,F})=\beta_{B,\operatorname{Res}_aF}$$
for every complex $F$ of $C$-module sheaves on $U$. Under these identifications the units and counits defining the inverse adjoint mates also agree: $\beta_B^{-1}$ is the $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ adjunct of
$$g_U^{-1}F\xrightarrow{g_U^{-1}u_F}g_U^{-1}j^{-1}j_!F\cong j'^{-1}g^{-1}j_!F,$$
where $u$ is the extension/restriction unit and the last map is the adjunction-compatible site-composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition]. All these assertions are natural in chain maps and in $a$, including identities and composites. In particular, for any sequence of finite rings $B_{n+1}\to B_n$ and complexes $F_n$ with strict $B_{n+1}$-linear maps $F_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}F_n$, the maps $\beta_{B_n,F_n}$ and their inverses commute with every transition and define inverse maps of the underlying strict towers of abelian sheaf complexes. They also do so as towers over a ring sheaf acting through compatible maps to the $(B_n)$ coefficient sheaves. No quasi-compactness or constructibility hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The coefficient square follows by specializing the proved naturality theorem proEtaleConstantInverseImageMap_naturality of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] to the coefficient homomorphism. The comparison pullRes is the inverse mate of the identity-on-sections direct image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. The mates correspondence unit and counit equations give pull_unit_counit. Identity and compatible ambient restriction isomorphisms are constructed sectionwise using the identity and composite restriction isomorphisms of modules; extensionality proves uniqueness. Identity coherence follows by applying the adjunction Hom equivalence to the pullback comparison, using the proved identity-on-sections formula for the direct-image comparison and naturality of the unit. Transposing once more under the open adjunction proves extension identity coherence. Composition coherence retains its stated plan.

proof.text: Use the proved scalarSectionsAt equivalences and identity-on-sections scalarRestrictionIso and scalarDirectImageIso from [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]. For an open immersion use literal openImmersionRestriction in the fixed-scalar model. Its coefficient square has identity direct-image mate, by the geometric adjunction triangle identity. The inverse-mate cube identity follows from mateEquiv_vcomp and naturality in the vertical transformations. Apply it first to the module-pullback/direct-image adjunctions, obtaining compatibility of pullRes with the coordinate comparisons. Invert this compatibility and apply the same cube identity to the extension/restriction adjunctions. The coordinate mates are isomorphisms by [lem-stage3-inverse-mate-equivalences]. The remaining fixed-scalar mate is exactly openExtensionScalarMap, invertible by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Thus the image of each openResMap component under scalarSectionsAt is invertible; the equivalence reflects isomorphisms. This proves invertibility of the specified mate, including the empty open. The unit and counit compatibilities are the standard mate equations.

proof.text: First prove compatibility of pullRes with moduleGComp. Apply the mates correspondence to both routes; moduleGComp is the conjugate of moduleRComp, and the direct-image/scalar comparisons are identities on sections. The resulting equality is sectionwise naturality of pullbackComp. Combine this compositor compatibility with transport along the equality of composite scheme morphisms and the specified formula for moduleSquareG, obtaining pullRes_square. The unit equation for the mates correspondence identifies singleBetaInv with the inverse mate of moduleSquareG.inv under the two open adjunctions, preserving the recorded normalization of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. Invert the outer pullRes components in pullRes_square to obtain a commuting cube of right-adjoint squares. Apply the inverse-mate cube identity to the four open adjunctions. Its left-adjoint cube is precisely the scalar compatibility of singleBetaInv with sourceRes and targetRes. Invert the finite exchange isomorphisms to obtain the forward exchange equality, and apply it degreewise to complexes.

proof.text: In Lean, beta is the inverse of asIso singleBetaInv, and betaC is its termwise lift to complexes. Its inverse component in degree i therefore reduces to singleBetaInvApp at F.X i. By the definition of singleBetaInvApp from [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change], this is exactly the transpose of the pulled-back open unit followed by the inverse moduleSquareG comparison. Thus inverse_unit_transpose follows definitionally, with no further mate calculation.

At sheaf level, specialize exchange_scalars_app at the target of a semilinear map. Inverting the B and C exchange isomorphisms gives the inverse scalar square. Naturality of beta_B and its inverse at the semilinear map, followed by the two scalar squares, proves exchange_transition_app. Read these equalities in each complex degree and on each section to prove exchange_transition. For the strict tower assertion, check the successor square in each complex degree and on each underlying section; resForget is the identity there, so exchange_transition gives exactly the equality. For the ambient tower assertion, use the same sectionwise equality and the proved identity-on-sections formula for ambientRes, which follows from its unique specification. Thus the successor squares hold as actual linear morphisms. NatTrans.ofOpSequence constructs the forward and inverse tower maps. The component inverse identities prove that they are inverse, and the naturality constructor extends the successor equalities to every tower arrow.

proof_origin.place: Y8 stage-3 completion: normalized open scalar mate invertibility by two transports through the fixed-scalar equivalences; exchange compatibility by compositor coherence and a third application of the inverse-mate cube identity, with the recorded inverse-unit normalization preserved. The identity and composition clauses retain their stated arguments; transition uses naturality, and the strict and ambient tower squares are checked degreewise on sections to avoid expanding complex functor compositions.

The statement is true and keeps the parent's coefficient category (constant finite commutative rings, small pro-etale sites). beta runs g^{-1}j_! -> j'_!g_U^{-1} as in the base-change node, and the stated inverse mate is the correct one. No qc or constructibility hypothesis is needed. Small cases checked: a=id, zero ring, U empty, U=X, g=id, one-level tower, Z/l^n quotient towers. Not a duplicate: the base-change node has one ring; the underived-compatibility node gives the same mate normalization but on the etale site; strict-tower-proper-open-calculus has one fixed ring B; and no clause of the parent is restated. Faults, both E5: step 3 transported beta summand by summand and invoked an unnamed uniqueness, and step 4 asserted the mate computation without doing it. The fix rewrites steps 1-4 only. Step 1 adds h_* and the units and counits of h^* -| h_*. Step 2 shows the units and adjuncts are ring-independent, citing the 03DI construction. Step 3 now uses the Beck-Chevalley characterization: beta is the unique map with adjunct t^{-1}eta_2, where t_{M,V}=M(a_V) and Res_a fixes t and the units. Step 4 computes the j'_!-adjunct of beta^{-1} as sigma o g_U^{-1}u_F, with sigma the mate of t, and identifies sigma with the composition comparison via clause (3) of lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition. I read the statement's 'canonical map' as the standard Beck-Chevalley exchange constructed in step 6 of the base-change node. The statement, stmt_deps and proof_deps union are unchanged, every step is under 2000 characters, and there is no cycle.
